criteria.description: When the API call succeeds, the optimistic favourite state change is kept — isFavourite(productId) returns true after a successful add and false after a successful remove.
criteria.evidence: favouriteRevert.test.tsx passed all 4 tests in 242ms. Tests 'clicking the favourite button marks a product as a favourite' and 'clicking a favourited button removes the favourite' both pass. Fetch is stubbed globally in tests/setup.ts with vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ ok: true, ... }) confirming mocked-success fetch. Full test run: 7 test files, 21 tests, all passed, exit 0.

criteria.description: When the API call fails (fetch rejects), the optimistic state change is reverted: if the product was being added it is removed from favouriteIds, and if it was being removed it is re-added.
criteria.evidence: FavouritesContext.tsx lines 75–85: catch block calls setFavouriteIds((prev) => { const next = new Set(prev); if (wasAdded) { next.delete(productId); } else { next.add(productId); } return next; }). When wasAdded===true the optimistic add is reverted (delete); when wasAdded===false the optimistic remove is reverted (add). TypeScript build exits 0: 'tsc -b && vite build' completed with 65 modules transformed, no type errors.

criteria.description: A failed toggle on product A does not alter the favourite state of product B. The revert must use a functional state updater (prev => ...) rather than a closed-over snapshot of favouriteIds.
criteria.evidence: FavouritesContext.tsx lines 76–84: catch block calls setFavouriteIds((prev) => { ... return next; }) using a functional updater with the 'prev' parameter, not the 'favouriteIds' variable captured at call time. This ensures concurrent state from other products is preserved in 'prev' rather than being lost from a stale snapshot.

criteria.description: setPendingIds is called to add productId to pendingIds before the fetch call begins, so isPending(productId) returns true while the request is in flight.
criteria.evidence: FavouritesContext.tsx line 61: setPendingIds((prev) => new Set(prev).add(productId)) appears before the try block at line 63, which contains the await fetch(...) calls. The pending id is set before any async operation begins.

criteria.description: setPendingIds is called to remove productId from pendingIds after the request completes — whether it succeeds or fails — so isPending(productId) returns false once the request is done. This cleanup must be in a finally block, not duplicated in both try and catch branches.
criteria.evidence: FavouritesContext.tsx lines 86–91: finally block calls setPendingIds((prev) => { const next = new Set(prev); next.delete(productId); return next; }). No equivalent setPendingIds cleanup call exists in the try block (lines 63–74) or the catch block (lines 75–85).

criteria.description: FavouriteButton is rendered with disabled attribute while the request is in flight, preventing double-click. No change to FavouriteButton.tsx is required — it already reads isPending(productId) and passes the result to disabled.
criteria.evidence: FavouriteButton.tsx contains 'const pending = isPending(productId)' and 'disabled={pending}' — consistent with the expected unmodified baseline. git diff --name-only HEAD returns empty (working tree clean). Requirements 4 and 5 confirm isPending returns true during the request and false after, which flows to disabled={pending} in the existing button.
